title: The initial Islet-1 blueprint
summary: The first public version of the blueprint: {{studies}} studies and {{findings}} findings, the Idea Graveyard, {{designs}} designs scored on five tests, and the five layers of checks.

title: Test delayed and reduced vascular oxygen support together
summary: Asks what happens to the graft's oxygen supply when new blood vessels connect late and carry less oxygen than hoped, both at once.

outcome.note: The blueprint now tests late-forming blood vessels and weaker oxygen delivery together, under both ways the cells release oxygen, and publishes the whole grid, so it shows where the oxygen margin runs out.

title: The published chance-of-working estimate does not compute the quantity it states, and omits failure modes the blueprint already documents
summary: Asks that the odds on the Blueprint page say exactly what they measure, how the three-design figure is worked out, and which checks they leave out.

outcome.note: The odds now define each step as a design still in the running clearing the next hurdle, give the reason for each hurdle's three-design figure, and name the lab checks that sit outside the four hurdles, so they cannot be read as the chance of a cure.

title: Measure endocrine function after the modelled oxygen bridge and during recovery
summary: Asks whether the cells that survive the 14-day low-oxygen window still release insulin and glucagon normally afterwards, and adds a side-by-side lab test during and after recovery.

outcome.note: The blueprint now tests whether the cells that survive the 14-day low-oxygen window after transplant still release insulin and glucagon normally during and after recovery, separating lost cells from weakened ones before counting the working dose.

title: Test whether cell-free product effluent has PD-L1-dependent functional activity
summary: Asks whether cell-free liquid conditioned by the engineered islet cells can suppress a separately stimulated immune response through the PD-L1 brake, and adds a controlled lab screen to test it.

outcome.note: The blueprint now adds a controlled lab check of whether liquid collected from around the engineered islet cells can calm a separate immune response on its own, alongside the existing tests of how much protective protein stays on the cells and how much is shed into the liquid.

title: Compare intermediate endocrine mixtures at measured functional output and graft burden
summary: Asks whether islet-cell mixes between the current 60:30:10 recipe and insulin-cells-only controls can cut tissue volume or oxygen need while keeping hormone regulation intact, and adds a staged lab comparison.

outcome.note: The blueprint now adds a staged lab comparison of a few in-between cell mixes against the current 60:30:10 recipe, to see whether a slightly bigger share of insulin-making cells could mean fewer cells are needed, without weakening the other islet cells' protection against low blood sugar. The 60:30:10 recipe stays unless new measurements justify a change.

title: A human immune model in each well to evaluate islet graft responses
summary: Asks whether a combined human immune and islet co-culture at Stage 1 could catch failure modes between immune cell types that split Stage-0 tests miss.

outcome.note: Adds open question OQ-017 and a Stage-1 note beside Readout 3 asking whether a combined human immune and islet co-culture can catch cross-talk between immune cell types that split Stage-0 tests miss, once donor-mismatch background and cluster recovery from the gel are qualified.

title: Two factual errors in the evidence records behind OQ-008 and GY-009
summary: Points out that Xu 2024 tested surface-anchored CD47 in non-islet models rather than stem-cell islets, and separates Hu 2023's primary human islet CD47 threshold from its stem-cell islet counts.

outcome.note: Reclassifies Xu 2024 from stem-cell islets to its actual non-islet immune, blood-stem-cell and endothelial models (nudging Design A's overall score from 0.1085 to 0.1084), removes Xu 2024 from Idea Graveyard rule GY-009, and separates Hu 2023's primary human islet CD47 threshold arm from its engineered stem-cell islet counts.

title: Design X is scored under one name but specified as two products
summary: Asks that every mention of Design X across the blueprint, tissue simulations and open questions state whether it refers to the scored insulin-gene edit or the unscored Stage-0 upgrade bundle.

outcome.note: Maps each blueprint table, tissue simulation and open question explicitly to either the scored Design X grid comparison (Design A plus one insulin-gene base edit on the 119 µm oxygen layer) or the unscored Stage-0 Design X upgrade bundle (100 µm oxygen layer and outer-ring Fas-ligand gel), and widens OQ-015 across Designs A, B and X.

title: Carrying the 68-hour oxygen-release half-life across a reformulated source lamina
summary: Points out that the 68-hour oxygen-release half-life comes from a 25 wt% silicone disk and may shift in denser 31.25 wt% and 46.39 wt% microbeads, requiring per-recipe testing and sensitivity bounds.

outcome.note: Reclassifies the 68-hour oxygen-release half-life as an unvalidated per-recipe target rather than a fixed material constant, publishes an 84-run sensitivity sweep showing the safe half-life window for both the 31.25 wt% and 46.39 wt% peroxide recipes, and requires Stage-0 particle-size and release-rate measurements for each recipe.

title: Qualify core knock-in cis/splicing boundaries, SLC30A8 hold, iCasp9 3D references and seed-line TYK2 sensitivity
summary: Adds early lab checks for nearby inflammatory genes, host-gene splicing and promoter silencing around the core DNA edits, keeps ZnT8 intact until proved safe for islet yield, and adds 3D safety-switch and 10,000-patient donor-line audits.

outcome.note: The blueprint now checks nearby genes, host-gene splicing and anti-silencing switches around its core DNA edits, holds off deleting the zinc transporter ZnT8 until stem-cell yield and insulin output are proved, audits three crystal structures of the safety switch, and tests how a naturally protective TYK2 donor cell line affects the 10,000-patient simulation.

title: Add post-adjunct depletion assays, ectopic CD55 complement gates and held Stage-0 challenger falsifiers
summary: Adds lab tests to check whether islet grafts stay protected after their temporary immune-calming gel proteins wear off, isolates any benefit of added CD55 without harming insulin release, and holds four candidate gene edits behind strict proof gates.

outcome.note: The Stage-0 lab contract now tests never-treated, gel-depleted and active grafts side by side once immune-calming gel proteins wear off, checks added CD55 on the exact same edited graft without disturbing endogenous CD59 insulin release, and holds four candidate edits (TYMS, NLRC5, endogenous CD274 and TXNIP) outside core designs behind strict pass rules.

title: Add a thrombomodulin module to counter IBMIR, which CD47 and HLA-E do not cover
summary: Asks to add a thrombomodulin gene-edit module to protect transplanted islet cells from early blood clotting and complement attack, and to split Test 3 into separate scores for immune cells and clotting.

outcome.note: The plan already includes local thrombomodulin and whole-blood clotting and complement checks; the cited studies do not establish added benefit from a permanent THBD gene edit or justify changing Test 3 scoring, and the planned graft still needs lab validation.

title: Empirical qualification of implanted-form CaO2 microbead oxygen kinetics for the Islet-1 slab geometry
summary: Asks to measure oxygen release, hydrogen peroxide levels, cell survival and insulin release for the oxygen-producing microbeads in the actual 350 µm implant slab before relying on the 68-hour model target.

outcome.note: IIP-0010 already requires testing each oxygen-bead recipe in its implanted form for particle size and oxygen release, alongside peroxide checks and IIP-0004 hormone-function tests; these lab measurements remain to be run.

title: Add two-strand knock-in splice-grammar census, Mode-B challenger comparators and UMI/RT-PCR isoform gates
summary: Maps unintended two-way RNA splicing and repeated DNA across the inserted protective genes, sets up one-change-at-a-time test sequences alongside the untouched reference designs, and adds calibrated RNA and safety-switch lab checks.

outcome.note: The blueprint now scans inserted DNA in both directions for unintended RNA splicing and repeated sequences, registers synthesis-ready one-change-at-a-time Stage-0 challenger sequences alongside the untouched reference donors across Loci 1, 3 and 4, and requires calibrated RNA recovery, host-gene 3′-end and orientation controls before any sequence change advances.
